processing_steps.method: melted in a high-frequency vacuum induction furnace and cast into an ingot
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: 50 kg capacity furnace; ingot diameter 150 mm.
Applied to the cast ingots before hot rolling.

processing_steps.method: hot rolling into rods followed by air cooling
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Hot rolled into rods with a diameter of 16 mm, then air-cooled to room temperature.

processing_steps.method: solution treatment followed by water quenching
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: This is the terminal processing step defining the sample (process_id proc_st-1050c-2h-wq); the water-quenched state was used for tensile, Charpy impact, EBSD and TEM characterization.

structures.overall_structure: After 1050 °C/2 h solution treatment + water quenching the C-1.2 steel (Fe30Mn11Al1.2C) is fully austenitic (single FCC phase) with no ferrite/BCC phase, containing a fine dispersion of κ-carbides precipitated in the austenite matrix.

phases_present.morphology: equiaxed austenite grains with abundant twin boundaries

precipitates.distribution: uniformly distributed in the austenite matrix
precipitates.coherency: coherent with the austenite matrix (SAED evidence)

phase_interfaces.coherence: coherent interface with the austenite matrix (evidenced by SAED); orientation relationship (001)κ || (001)γ

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Fractional twin boundary length f_Tw = 51.8% for C-1.2; twin boundaries are present within the coarse austenite grains.

interfaces.slip_behavior: κ-carbide strengthening operates by a particle shear (shear hardening) mechanism rather than Orowan; shear deformation facilitates glide of dislocations across κ-carbide shear planes, weakening the work hardening rate (relevant to the coarse κ-carbides in the higher-C steels).
interfaces.phase_evolution: κ-carbides coarsen with increasing C content (from <1 nm at 0.6 %C, about 2.0 nm at 1.0 %C, ~20–25 nm at 1.2 %C, to ~50–80 nm at 1.5 %C).

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: round tensile specimen, gauge length 25 mm and diameter 5 mm, tensile axis parallel to the rod axis; Charpy impact specimen with V-notch perpendicular to the rod axis (10×10 mm cross-section, 2 mm deep notch)
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Charpy impact tests performed at −40 °C using an MTS impact tester (500 J capacity); data are average values of two specimens.

ultimate_tensile_strength.type: ultimate true stress σ_TS (maximum true stress just before necking)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: EBSD system attached to a field emission gun SEM (FEI Quanta 650, Thermo Fisher Scientific); Channel 5 post-processing software
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Operating voltage 20 kV, step size 0.5 μm; specimens mechanically ground then electro-polished in 7% Nital; grain size by linear intercept with 15° misorientation boundary definition
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine phase distribution (FCC austenite / BCC ferrite), grain size and twin boundaries as a function of alloying content
characterization_methods.key_findings: C-1.2 shows only austenite (no ferrite); average austenite grain size 22.5 ± 1.4 μm; fractional twin boundary length f_Tw = 51.8%.

characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) incl. dark-field imaging and SAED
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: TEM Tecnai G2 F20 S-TWIN, Thermo Fisher Scientific, operated at 200 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Thin foils prepared by twin-jet electro-polishing in a mixture of 10% perchloric acid and 90% ethanol at 20 V and −20 °C; dark-field images taken along [001]γ zone axis using a κ-carbide reflection
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize the size, distribution and orientation relationship of κ-carbide precipitates in the austenite matrix
characterization_methods.key_findings: κ-carbides present and coarsen with C content; for the 1.2 %C steel resolvable bright κ-carbide particles are uniformly distributed (Table 3 gives 20 ± 6 nm); orientation relationship (001)κ || (001)γ.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Initial strain rate 1.1×10^-3 s^-1 at ambient temperature; round specimens 25 mm gauge length / 5 mm diameter with axis parallel to rod axis
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure engineering stress-strain response, yield strength, tensile strength and ductility

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Tested at −40 °C; V-notch perpendicular to the rod axis; average of two specimens
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure impact toughness of the solution-treated steels

unmapped_findings: κ-carbide size reported for the 1.2 %C steel: text (b0044) states 'The average diameter of the κ-carbides was measured as about 25 nm for the 1.2%C steel', whereas Table 3 (b0047) lists 20 ± 6 nm for C-1.2; the text value (25 nm) and the tabulated value (20 ± 6 nm) differ.
Only austenite (no BCC ferrite) is present in the 1.2 %C steel after 1050 °C/2 h solution treatment (b0043).
For the Fe30Mn11Al(x)C series the yield strength increases from 542 MPa to 1125 MPa as C is raised from 0.6% to 1.5%, accompanied by a decrease in tensile elongation from ~60% to ~20% (b0025).
The κ-carbides in the 1.2 %C steel show a resolvable bright contrast in dark-field TEM (panels (g) of Fig. 3) with stronger κ reflections in the SAED pattern than at lower C (figure_003).
General finding across all compositions: σ_TS (ultimate true stress) ≈ 1350 MPa and σ_FS (fracture strength) ≈ 2150 MPa are nearly independent of C, Mn and Al content (b0040, b0075, b0083).
General density relationship: ρ = 8.1 − 0.102C − 0.10Al − 0.01Mn (g/cm³, alloy content in mass%) (b0063, b0081).
